## Dumbbell chart (`dumbbell-chart`)
Change per item as two dots joined by a line: before and after, plan and actual. Green when good, red when bad.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Change per item, shown as two dots joined by a line.
- How to read it: The hollow dot is the earlier value, the filled dot the later one. A longer line means a bigger change. Green means a good change, red a bad one.
- Use it for: Before and after, plan vs actual, this year vs last year across many items.
- Skip it when: More than two moments in time (use lines), or a single item.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add dumbbell-chart`
- Import: `import { DumbbellChart } from '@/components/ui/dumbbell-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { DumbbellChart } from '@/components/ui/dumbbell-chart';

export default function DumbbellChartDemo() {
  return (
    <DumbbellChart
      className="w-[34rem] max-w-full"
      fromLabel="2025"
      toLabel="2026"
      format={(n) => `${n}%`}
      rows={[
        { label: 'Engineering', from: 62, to: 78 },
        { label: 'Sales', from: 71, to: 69 },
        { label: 'Support', from: 55, to: 74 },
        { label: 'Marketing', from: 68, to: 81 },
        { label: 'Finance', from: 80, to: 77 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## File manager (`file-manager`)
Folder browser with breadcrumb, list and grid views, selection and double-click or Enter to open.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add file-manager`
- Import: `import { FileManager } from '@/components/ui/file-manager'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { FileManager, type FileItem } from '@/components/ui/file-manager';

const tree: Record<string, FileItem[]> = {
  '': [
    { id: 'hr', name: 'HR', type: 'folder', modified: '07 Oct' },
    { id: 'fin', name: 'Finance', type: 'folder', modified: '05 Oct' },
    { id: 'brand', name: 'Brand assets', type: 'folder', modified: '28 Sep' },
    { id: 'readme', name: 'Welcome.pdf', type: 'file', size: 482000, modified: '01 Sep' },
  ],
  hr: [
    { id: 'policy', name: 'Leave policy 2026.pdf', type: 'file', size: 910000, modified: '06 Oct' },
    { id: 'offer', name: 'Offer letter template.docx', type: 'file', size: 64000, modified: '02 Oct' },
    { id: 'org', name: 'Org chart.png', type: 'image', size: 1840000, modified: '30 Sep' },
  ],
  fin: [
    { id: 'p', name: 'Payroll September.xlsx', type: 'file', size: 233000, modified: '05 Oct' },
    { id: 'inv', name: 'Invoices', type: 'folder', modified: '03 Oct' },
  ],
  brand: [
    { id: 'logo', name: 'Logo.png', type: 'image', size: 54000, modified: '12 Sep' },
    { id: 'guide', name: 'Brand guide.pdf', type: 'file', size: 5200000, modified: '12 Sep' },
  ],
  inv: [{ id: 'i1', name: 'INV-204.pdf', type: 'file', size: 88000, modified: '03 Oct' }],
};

export default function FileManagerDemo() {
  const [trail, setTrail] = React.useState<{ id: string; name: string }[]>([]);
  const here = trail.length ? trail[trail.length - 1].id : '';
  return (
    <FileManager
      className="max-w-xl"
      path={['Files', ...trail.map((t) => t.name)]}
      items={tree[here] ?? []}
      onNavigate={(d) => setTrail(trail.slice(0, d))}
      onOpen={(it) => it.type === 'folder' && setTrail([...trail, { id: it.id, name: it.name }])}
    />
  );
}
```

## Forecast chart (`forecast-chart`)
Solid line for what happened, dashed line inside a shaded band for what is expected. The band is the likely range.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: What happened so far, plus what we expect next with a range around it.
- How to read it: The solid line is real data. After the vertical divider the dashed line is the prediction and the shaded band is the likely range. A wider band means less certainty.
- Use it for: Revenue, demand or headcount projections where you want to show uncertainty honestly.
- Skip it when: Predictions with no real uncertainty estimate: a band you made up is worse than a plain dashed line.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add forecast-chart`
- Import: `import { ForecastChart } from '@/components/ui/forecast-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ForecastChart } from '@/components/ui/forecast-chart';

export default function ForecastChartDemo() {
  return (
    <ForecastChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      format={(n) => `₹${n}L`}
      labels={['Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec', 'Jan', 'Feb']}
      actual={[42, 48, 45, 58, 63, 61, 72]}
      forecast={[76, 81, 84, 90]}
      low={[72, 74, 74, 77]}
      high={[80, 88, 94, 103]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Funnel chart (`funnel-chart`)
Conversion funnel with a bar per stage and the step-to-step rate.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How many people drop off at each step of a process.
- How to read it: Each bar is a step, widest first. The gap between two bars is the drop-off. The percentage is how many made it from the step before.
- Use it for: Signup flow, sales pipeline, checkout steps.
- Skip it when: Steps that are not in order, or processes where people can skip steps.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add funnel-chart`
- Import: `import { FunnelChart } from '@/components/ui/funnel-chart'`

Example:

```tsx
import { FunnelChart } from '@/components/ui/funnel-chart';

export default function FunnelChartDemo() {
  return <FunnelChart className="max-w-xl" stages={[{ label: 'Visitors', value: 48200 }, { label: 'Sign-ups', value: 9640 }, { label: 'Qualified', value: 3120 }, { label: 'Demo booked', value: 1210 }, { label: 'Won', value: 340 }]} />;
}
```

## Gantt chart (`gantt`)
Schedule view with a bar per task, progress fill, weekend shading and a today line.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Tasks as bars on a calendar, so you see when each starts, ends and overlaps.
- How to read it: Each row is a task. The bar runs from its start to its end date. The filled part is progress. The vertical line is today.
- Use it for: Project plans, roadmaps, team schedules.
- Skip it when: Tasks without dates, or very large plans (use a roadmap board).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add gantt`
- Import: `import { Gantt } from '@/components/ui/gantt'`

Example:

```tsx
import { Gantt, type GanttTask } from '@/components/ui/gantt';

const d = (offset: number) => { const t = new Date(); t.setDate(t.getDate() + offset); return `${t.getFullYear()}-${String(t.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(t.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`; };

const tasks: GanttTask[] = [
  { id: '1', name: 'Discovery', owner: 'Isha Nair', start: d(-10), end: d(-4), progress: 100, tone: 'success' },
  { id: '2', name: 'Design system', owner: 'Diya Rao', start: d(-6), end: d(3), progress: 70, tone: 'info' },
  { id: '3', name: 'Backend APIs', owner: 'Rohan Das', start: d(-3), end: d(9), progress: 40 },
  { id: '4', name: 'Frontend build', owner: 'Aarav Mehta', start: d(1), end: d(14), progress: 10 },
  { id: '5', name: 'QA and fixes', owner: 'Vikram Joshi', start: d(10), end: d(18), progress: 0, tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '6', name: 'Launch', owner: 'Meera Iyer', start: d(19), end: d(21), progress: 0, tone: 'danger' },
];

export default function GanttDemo() {
  return <Gantt tasks={tasks} />;
}
```

## Gauge (`gauge`)
Half-circle meter with a needle that swings to the value.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One number against a range, like a car speedometer.
- How to read it: The needle and filled arc show where the value sits between the minimum and maximum. Colored zones tell you if that is good, so a needle in green is fine.
- Use it for: A single health score, CPU load, quota used.
- Skip it when: More than one measure, or precise values. Pair with the number printed in the middle.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add gauge`
- Import: `import { Gauge } from '@/components/ui/gauge'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Gauge } from '@/components/ui/gauge';
import { Slider } from '@/components/ui/slider';

export default function GaugeDemo() {
  const [v, setV] = React.useState(72);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-4">
      <Gauge value={v} label="Team engagement" />
      <Slider aria-label="Gauge value" className="w-56" value={v} onValueChange={setV} showValue={false} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Half donut chart (`half-donut-chart`)
A semicircle split into parts with a total under the arch. Half the height of a donut, so it fits dashboard cards.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A semicircle split into parts, with a total or headline number under the arch.
- How to read it: The full arch is the whole (or the maximum if you set one). Each colored arc is one part. An empty stretch at the end is the unused part.
- Use it for: Budget used, storage by file type, seats by group, a dashboard card with little height.
- Skip it when: Many parts, or values that need precise comparison.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add half-donut-chart`
- Import: `import { HalfDonutChart } from '@/components/ui/half-donut-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { HalfDonutChart } from '@/components/ui/half-donut-chart';

export default function HalfDonutChartDemo() {
  return <HalfDonutChart max={200} format={(n) => `${n} GB`} data={[{ label: 'Documents', value: 62 }, { label: 'Photos', value: 48 }, { label: 'Backups', value: 31, color: 'text-warning' }]} />;
}
```

## Heatmap (`heatmap`)
Contribution-style grid for daily activity. Cells pop in column by column.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Activity per day over many weeks, like the GitHub contribution graph.
- How to read it: Each square is a day. Darker means more activity. Each column is a week and each row is a weekday, so streaks look like dark lines.
- Use it for: Check-ins, commits, support tickets per day, habit tracking.
- Skip it when: Short spans of a few days, or when exact counts matter (hover shows them, but a table is clearer).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add heatmap`
- Import: `import { Heatmap } from '@/components/ui/heatmap'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Heatmap } from '@/components/ui/heatmap';

export default function HeatmapDemo() {
  // Deterministic pseudo-random so the demo looks the same every time.
  const values = React.useMemo(() => Array.from({ length: 26 * 7 }, (_, i) => {
    const x = Math.sin(i * 12.9898) * 43758.5453;
    const r = x - Math.floor(x);
    const weekend = i % 7 === 0 || i % 7 === 6;
    return r < (weekend ? 0.6 : 0.2) ? 0 : Math.floor(r * 12);
  }), []);
  return <Heatmap values={values} unit="check-ins" />;
}
```

## Histogram chart (`histogram-chart`)
Counts how many values fall in each range from raw data, with a smooth curve over the bars. Bars rise in turn.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How many values fall into each range.
- How to read it: Each bar is a range of values. Taller means more values land there. The shape tells you the story: a hill in the middle is typical, a long tail means a few big values, two humps mean two groups.
- Use it for: Order sizes, response times, ages, exam scores.
- Skip it when: Categories (use a bar chart), or fewer than about 30 values.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add histogram-chart`
- Import: `import { HistogramChart } from '@/components/ui/histogram-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { HistogramChart } from '@/components/ui/histogram-chart';

// Deterministic pseudo-random bell-ish values so the demo looks the same every time.
const rnd = (i: number) => { const x = Math.sin(i * 12.9898) * 43758.5453; return x - Math.floor(x); };

export default function HistogramChartDemo() {
  const values = React.useMemo(() => Array.from({ length: 400 }, (_, i) => Math.round(2400 + (rnd(i) + rnd(i + 400) + rnd(i + 800) - 1.5) * 1900)), []);
  return <HistogramChart className="w-[36rem] max-w-full" values={values} bins={14} format={(n) => `₹${Math.round(n)}`} />;
}
```

## Kanban board (`kanban`)
Columns of draggable cards. Drag with the mouse or move a focused card with Alt and the arrow keys. Controlled, no drag library.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add kanban`
- Import: `import { Kanban } from '@/components/ui/kanban'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/avatar';
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge';
import { Kanban, type KanbanColumn } from '@/components/ui/kanban';

interface Task { id: string; title: string; tag: string; owner: string; due: string }

const columns: KanbanColumn[] = [
  { id: 'todo', title: 'To do', tone: 'default' },
  { id: 'doing', title: 'In progress', tone: 'info' },
  { id: 'review', title: 'In review', tone: 'warning' },
  { id: 'done', title: 'Done', tone: 'success' },
];

const tagTone = { Bug: 'danger', Feature: 'info', Chore: 'default', Design: 'warning' } as const;

export default function KanbanDemo() {
  const [board, setBoard] = React.useState<Record<string, Task[]>>({
    todo: [
      { id: 't1', title: 'Onboarding checklist for new hires', tag: 'Feature', owner: 'Isha Nair', due: '14 Oct' },
      { id: 't2', title: 'Fix payslip PDF margins', tag: 'Bug', owner: 'Rohan Das', due: '12 Oct' },
      { id: 't3', title: 'Archive 2023 attendance logs', tag: 'Chore', owner: 'Meera Iyer', due: '30 Oct' },
    ],
    doing: [
      { id: 't4', title: 'Leave balance widget', tag: 'Feature', owner: 'Aarav Mehta', due: '16 Oct' },
      { id: 't5', title: 'Refresh login screen', tag: 'Design', owner: 'Diya Rao', due: '15 Oct' },
    ],
    review: [{ id: 't6', title: 'Holiday calendar import', tag: 'Feature', owner: 'Kabir Shah', due: '11 Oct' }],
    done: [
      { id: 't7', title: 'Dark mode for dashboards', tag: 'Design', owner: 'Diya Rao', due: '03 Oct' },
      { id: 't8', title: 'Duplicate employee IDs', tag: 'Bug', owner: 'Vikram Joshi', due: '05 Oct' },
    ],
  });
  return (
    <Kanban
      columns={columns}
      value={board}
      onChange={setBoard}
      renderCard={(t) => (
        <div className="grid gap-2">
          <p className="font-medium leading-snug">{t.title}</p>
          <div className="flex items-center justify-between gap-2">
            <Badge variant={tagTone[t.tag as keyof typeof tagTone]}>{t.tag}</Badge>
            <span className="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs text-muted-foreground">{t.due}<Avatar name={t.owner} size="xs" /></span>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    />
  );
}
```

## Line chart (`line-chart`)
Multi-series line or area chart in plain SVG with grid, axis labels, legend and a hover readout.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How one or more numbers change over time.
- How to read it: Left to right is time. Higher is more. A line going up is growth, down is decline. Hover to read exact values.
- Use it for: Revenue by month, signups by week, anything where the trend matters more than any single point.
- Skip it when: Comparing categories with no time order (use bars), or fewer than 4 points (a stat card says it better).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add line-chart`
- Import: `import { LineChart } from '@/components/ui/line-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { LineChart } from '@/components/ui/line-chart';

const months = ['Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct'];

export default function LineChartDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl gap-8">
      <LineChart
        area
        labels={months}
        format={(n) => `₹${n}L`}
        series={[
          { name: 'Revenue', data: [42, 48, 45, 58, 63, 61, 72] },
          { name: 'Payroll', data: [30, 31, 31, 34, 36, 36, 38], color: 'text-warning' },
          { name: 'Profit', data: [12, 17, 14, 24, 27, 25, 34], color: 'text-success' },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Live chart (`live-chart`)
Streaming line chart that slides left as new values arrive. You give it a function for the next value; pause it any time.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A line that keeps moving as fresh numbers arrive, like a heart-rate monitor.
- How to read it: The right edge is now; older values slide off to the left. The tag at the top right is the latest value.
- Use it for: Active users right now, requests per second, CPU, queue length.
- Skip it when: Historical analysis. It forgets old points; use a line or area chart for a full history.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add live-chart`
- Import: `import { LiveChart } from '@/components/ui/live-chart'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { LiveChart } from '@/components/ui/live-chart';

export default function LiveChartDemo() {
  const [paused, setPaused] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-3">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between"><span className="text-sm font-medium">Active users</span><Button size="xs" variant="outline" onClick={() => setPaused(!paused)}>{paused ? 'Resume' : 'Pause'}</Button></div>
      <LiveChart paused={paused} next={(p) => Math.max(10, Math.min(95, p + (Math.random() - 0.5) * 14))} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Lollipop chart (`lollipop-chart`)
A bar chart as a thin stick with a dot on the end, sorted largest first. Lighter than bars when there are many items.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A bar chart drawn with a thin stick and a dot. Same message, less ink.
- How to read it: The further the dot from the left, the bigger the value. Sorted biggest first so the ranking reads from the top.
- Use it for: Many items to rank: tickets per customer, bugs per module.
- Skip it when: Only two or three items: a plain bar is fine.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add lollipop-chart`
- Import: `import { LollipopChart } from '@/components/ui/lollipop-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

```tsx
        { label: 'Billing', value: 12 }, { label: 'Onboarding', value: 8 }, { label: 'Reports', value: 21 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Marimekko chart (`marimekko-chart`)
Stacked 100% bars whose widths also mean something: column width is group size, block height is mix. Columns grow up on scroll.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Stacked 100% bars where the width of each column is also data. Also called a mosaic or Mekko chart.
- How to read it: Column width is how big that group is. Block height is the mix inside it. A block's area is its share of everything. Hover a block for both percentages.
- Use it for: Market share by region (wide regions are bigger markets), plan mix per customer segment.
- Skip it when: More than five blocks per column, or when widths do not carry meaning: use a stacked bar chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add marimekko-chart`
- Import: `import { MarimekkoChart } from '@/components/ui/marimekko-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { MarimekkoChart } from '@/components/ui/marimekko-chart';

export default function MarimekkoChartDemo() {
  return (
    <MarimekkoChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      format={(n) => `₹${n}L`}
      keys={[{ key: 'pro', label: 'Pro' }, { key: 'biz', label: 'Business', color: 'text-success' }, { key: 'starter', label: 'Starter', color: 'text-warning' }]}
      columns={[
        { label: 'North', values: { pro: 40, biz: 30, starter: 10 } },
        { label: 'West', values: { pro: 55, biz: 50, starter: 20 } },
        { label: 'South', values: { pro: 30, biz: 20, starter: 25 } },
        { label: 'East', values: { pro: 10, biz: 8, starter: 12 } },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Matrix heatmap (`matrix-heatmap`)
Rows by columns shaded by value: traffic by hour and weekday, cohort retention. Cells fade in as a wave; hover lights up the row and column.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A grid where the color of each cell shows a value: rows by columns.
- How to read it: Find a row and a column, read the cell where they meet. Darker or brighter means a bigger number. Look for bright clusters and dark gaps.
- Use it for: Traffic by hour and weekday, cohort retention by month, errors by service and day.
- Skip it when: When you need to compare exact values (colors are hard to compare closely), or hundreds of rows. Turn on showValues to print the numbers.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add matrix-heatmap`
- Import: `import { MatrixHeatmap } from '@/components/ui/matrix-heatmap'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { MatrixHeatmap } from '@/components/ui/matrix-heatmap';

const rows = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun'];
const cols = ['6a', '8a', '10a', '12p', '2p', '4p', '6p', '8p', '10p'];
// Busy weekday mid-mornings and afternoons, quiet weekends.
const values = rows.map((_, r) => cols.map((_, c) => Math.round((r > 4 ? 6 : 20) * (1 + Math.sin((c + 1) * 0.9) * 0.8) + ((r * 7 + c * 13) % 9))));

export default function MatrixHeatmapDemo() {
  return <MatrixHeatmap className="w-full max-w-xl" rows={rows} cols={cols} values={values} showValues format={(n) => String(Math.max(0, n))} />;
}
```

## Pareto chart (`pareto-chart`)
Causes sorted by size as bars plus a running-total line with an 80% mark. Shows which few causes matter most.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Causes sorted biggest to smallest as bars, plus a running-total line.
- How to read it: Read the bars left to right: the biggest cause first. The line shows the running percent of the total. Where it crosses the dashed 80% line is how many causes make up most of the problem.
- Use it for: Finding the few causes behind most defects, tickets or costs (the 80/20 rule).
- Skip it when: Items that are not causes of one total, or fewer than five items.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pareto-chart`
- Import: `import { ParetoChart } from '@/components/ui/pareto-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import { ParetoChart } from '@/components/ui/pareto-chart';

export default function ParetoChartDemo() {
  return (
    <ParetoChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      items={[
        { label: 'Login', value: 142 }, { label: 'Billing', value: 96 }, { label: 'Slow', value: 61 }, { label: 'Export', value: 28 },
        { label: 'Mobile', value: 17 }, { label: 'Search', value: 11 }, { label: 'Other', value: 9 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Permission matrix (`permission-matrix`)
Roles by permissions grid of checkboxes with per-column toggle and locked roles.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add permission-matrix`
- Import: `import { PermissionMatrix } from '@/components/ui/permission-matrix'`
- Also needs: checkbox, table

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { PermissionMatrix, type Grants } from '@/components/ui/permission-matrix';

const roles = [
  { id: 'owner', label: 'Owner', hint: 'Always full access' },
  { id: 'admin', label: 'Admin', hint: 'Manages people and settings' },
  { id: 'finance', label: 'Finance', hint: 'Invoices and payouts' },
  { id: 'manager', label: 'Manager', hint: 'Own team only' },
  { id: 'support', label: 'Support', hint: 'Customer tickets' },
  { id: 'viewer', label: 'Viewer', hint: 'Read-only' },
];
const permissions = [
  { id: 'view', label: 'View' },
  { id: 'create', label: 'Create' },
  { id: 'edit', label: 'Edit' },
  { id: 'delete', label: 'Delete' },
  { id: 'approve', label: 'Approve' },
  { id: 'export', label: 'Export' },
  { id: 'billing', label: 'Billing' },
];

export default function PermissionMatrixDemo() {
  const [grants, setGrants] = React.useState<Grants>({
    owner: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'delete', 'approve', 'export', 'billing'],
    admin: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'delete', 'approve', 'export'],
    finance: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'approve', 'export', 'billing'],
    manager: ['view', 'create', 'edit', 'approve'],
    support: ['view', 'create', 'edit'],
    viewer: ['view'],
  });
  return <PermissionMatrix className="w-full max-w-3xl" roles={roles} permissions={permissions} value={grants} onChange={setGrants} locked={['owner']} />;
}
```

## Pie chart (`pie-chart`)
Slices of one whole that sweep around on scroll. Hover a slice or legend row and it pulls out.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One whole divided into slices.
- How to read it: A bigger slice is a bigger share. The slices add up to 100%. Hover a slice to pull it out and see the value.
- Use it for: Three to five parts of a whole: plan mix, traffic by source.
- Skip it when: Many slices, similar-sized slices (hard to tell apart), or comparing across several pies. Use a bar chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pie-chart`
- Import: `import { PieChart } from '@/components/ui/pie-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

```tsx
    />
  );
}
```

## Pivot table (`pivot-table`)
Cross-tab of your rows: one field down the side, another across the top, sum, count, average, min or max in each cell, with totals and heat shading.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pivot-table`
- Import: `import { PivotTable } from '@/components/ui/pivot-table'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { PivotTable } from '@/components/ui/pivot-table';
import { Segmented } from '@/components/ui/segmented';

const regions = ['North', 'South', 'West', 'East'];
const quarters = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4'];
const products = ['Starter', 'Growth', 'Scale'];
const sales = regions.flatMap((region, i) => quarters.flatMap((quarter, j) => products.map((product, k) => ({ region, quarter, product, revenue: ((i + 2) * (j + 3) * (k + 1) * 37_000) % 900_000 + 120_000 }))));

export default function PivotTableDemo() {
  const [by, setBy] = React.useState<'quarter' | 'product'>('quarter');
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full gap-4">
      <Segmented value={by} onValueChange={setBy} options={[{ value: 'quarter', label: 'By quarter' }, { value: 'product', label: 'By product' }]} />
      <PivotTable data={sales} rows="region" columns={by} value="revenue" rowLabel="Region" format={(n) => `₹${(n / 100_000).toFixed(1)}L`} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Progress ring (`progress-ring`)
Circular progress with an eased stroke animation.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One percentage shown as a circle that fills up.
- How to read it: A full circle is 100%. The number in the middle is the exact value.
- Use it for: Profile completion, upload progress, a single KPI vs target.
- Skip it when: Several values at once: use radial-bar-chart or a progress bar list.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add progress-ring`
- Import: `import { ProgressRing } from '@/components/ui/progress-ring'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { ProgressRing } from '@/components/ui/progress-ring';

export default function ProgressRingDemo() {
  const [v, setV] = React.useState(0);
  React.useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => setV(72), 100); return () => clearTimeout(t); }, []);
  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-8">
      <ProgressRing value={v} aria-label="Upload progress" />
      <ProgressRing value={v / 2} aria-label="Setup progress" size={72} stroke={6} className="text-success" />
      <button className="text-sm text-primary hover:underline" onClick={() => setV((x) => (x === 72 ? 30 : 72))}>Animate</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Punch card chart (`punch-card-chart`)
A grid of dots where dot size is the value, like commits by weekday and hour. Dots pop in on a diagonal wave.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A grid of dots where the size of a dot is the value.
- How to read it: Find a row and a column; a bigger dot where they meet is a bigger value. Look for rows or columns with big dots in a line.
- Use it for: Commits by weekday and hour, tickets by day and shift, orders by slot. Smaller grids than a heatmap.
- Skip it when: Large grids over about 10 by 24, where dots blur together. Use a matrix heatmap.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add punch-card-chart`
- Import: `import { PunchCardChart } from '@/components/ui/punch-card-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { PunchCardChart } from '@/components/ui/punch-card-chart';

const rows = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed', 'Thu', 'Fri', 'Sat', 'Sun'];
const cols = ['6a', '8a', '10a', '12p', '2p', '4p', '6p', '8p', '10p'];
const values = rows.map((_, r) => cols.map((_, c) => Math.max(0, Math.round((r > 4 ? 4 : 18) * (1 + Math.sin((c + 1) * 0.9) * 0.9) + ((r * 5 + c * 11) % 7) - 3))));

export default function PunchCardChartDemo() {
  return <PunchCardChart className="w-[34rem] max-w-full" rows={rows} cols={cols} values={values} format={(n) => `${n} commits`} />;
}
```

## Radar chart (`radar-chart`)
Spider chart for several scores on the same axes: a pentagon with five, a hexagon with six. Shapes grow from the center on scroll; hover a legend name to highlight a series.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Several scores for one thing on the same scale, drawn as a polygon. With five axes it is a pentagon, with six a hexagon. Also called a spider or web chart.
- How to read it: Each spoke is one skill or measure; the further the corner from the center, the higher the score. A big, even shape is well rounded; a lopsided shape has a weak spot. Compare shapes, not exact numbers.
- Use it for: Skill profiles, team reviews, product vs competitor on 5 to 8 qualities, player stats.
- Skip it when: Axes that are not on the same scale, more than 8 axes, or more than 3 shapes at once. Use bars when exact comparison matters.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add radar-chart`
- Import: `import { RadarChart } from '@/components/ui/radar-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { RadarChart } from '@/components/ui/radar-chart';

/** Five axes make a pentagon; add or remove an axis and the shape follows. */
export default function RadarChartDemo() {
  return (
    <RadarChart
      axes={['Delivery', 'Quality', 'Communication', 'Ownership', 'Teamwork']}
      series={[
        { name: 'Aarav', values: [88, 82, 70, 90, 76] },
        { name: 'Team average', values: [72, 74, 78, 68, 80] },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Radial bar chart (`radial-bar-chart`)
Concentric rings, one per goal, that sweep in on scroll. Legend hover highlights a ring; the middle takes any content.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Several progress rings nested inside each other, one ring per goal.
- How to read it: A ring is full at the target (100%). A longer arc means closer to the goal. Outer rings are longer, so compare the percentages, not the arc length.
- Use it for: Goals vs target on a dashboard: calls, revenue, tickets closed. Fitness-style activity rings.
- Skip it when: Comparing raw values across rings, or more than five rings.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add radial-bar-chart`
- Import: `import { RadialBarChart } from '@/components/ui/radial-bar-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { RadialBarChart } from '@/components/ui/radial-bar-chart';

export default function RadialBarChartDemo() {
  return (
    <RadialBarChart
      className="w-full max-w-sm"
      data={[{ label: 'Revenue', value: 82 }, { label: 'New leads', value: 64 }, { label: 'Tickets closed', value: 91 }, { label: 'NPS', value: 48 }]}
    >
      <div className="grid"><span className="text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums">71%</span><span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">of target</span></div>
    </RadialBarChart>
  );
}
```

## Radial line chart (`radial-line-chart`)
A line chart bent into a circle for things that repeat: 24 hours, 12 months. A smooth closed shape grows from the middle.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A line chart bent into a circle so the end meets the start. Good for things that repeat.
- How to read it: Each spoke is one label, like an hour or a month. Distance from the center is the value. A bulge shows a busy period. Move over the chart to read the nearest spoke.
- Use it for: 24 hours, 12 months or 7 weekdays: traffic by hour, sales by month.
- Skip it when: Data that does not repeat (the start and end join, which is misleading), or exact comparison. Use a line chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add radial-line-chart`
- Import: `import { RadialLineChart } from '@/components/ui/radial-line-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { RadialLineChart } from '@/components/ui/radial-line-chart';

export default function RadialLineChartDemo() {
  const hours = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => `${h}`);
  const day = (peak: number, width: number, height: number) => hours.map((_, h) => { const d = Math.min(Math.abs(h - peak), 24 - Math.abs(h - peak)); return Math.round(6 + height * Math.exp(-(d * d) / (2 * width * width))); });
  return <RadialLineChart labels={hours} format={(n) => `${n} req/s`} series={[{ name: 'Web', data: day(14, 3.2, 90) }, { name: 'Mobile', data: day(21, 2.4, 70), color: 'text-success' }]} />;
}
```

## Ridgeline chart (`ridgeline-chart`)
One smooth curve per row, overlapping like mountain ridges on a shared scale. Ridges rise in turn; hover one to bring it forward.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: One curve per row, stacked so they overlap like mountain ridges. All rows share one scale.
- How to read it: Each row is one group. A high peak is a busy moment. Look at where each ridge peaks to compare groups. Overlap is on purpose.
- Use it for: Activity by hour for several teams, score distributions per class, seasonality per city.
- Skip it when: Exact values, or more than about 8 rows. For one group use an area chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add ridgeline-chart`
- Import: `import { RidgelineChart } from '@/components/ui/ridgeline-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import { RidgelineChart } from '@/components/ui/ridgeline-chart';

export default function RidgelineChartDemo() {
  const hours = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => `${h}h`);
  const peak = (center: number, width: number, height: number) => hours.map((_, h) => Math.round(height * Math.exp(-((h - center) ** 2) / (2 * width ** 2)) + 3));
  return (
    <RidgelineChart
      className="w-[38rem] max-w-full"
      labels={hours}
      series={[
        { name: 'Support', data: peak(11, 3, 60) },
        { name: 'Sales', data: peak(14, 2.5, 80) },
        { name: 'Engineering', data: peak(16, 4, 50) },
        { name: 'Ops', data: peak(21, 2, 70) },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Rose chart (`rose-chart`)
Polar area chart: equal-angle petals whose length is the value. Petals bloom from the center in turn; hover one to read it.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Petals around a circle where the length of each petal is a value. Also called a polar area or Nightingale chart.
- How to read it: Each petal is one category, in order around the circle. A longer petal is a bigger value. Length is scaled so area matches the value, so small differences look small.
- Use it for: Seasonal data: sales by month, incidents by hour or weekday.
- Skip it when: Comparing precise values: bars are easier to read. Not for data that has no cycle or order.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add rose-chart`
- Import: `import { RoseChart } from '@/components/ui/rose-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { RoseChart } from '@/components/ui/rose-chart';

export default function RoseChartDemo() {
  const months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec'];
  const sales = [32, 28, 41, 55, 62, 48, 39, 44, 70, 83, 66, 91];
  return <RoseChart data={months.map((label, i) => ({ label, value: sales[i]!, color: i % 3 === 0 ? 'text-primary' : i % 3 === 1 ? 'text-success' : 'text-info' }))} format={(n) => `₹${n}L`} />;
}
```

## Sankey chart (`sankey-chart`)
Flow diagram where ribbon width is the amount: traffic to page to outcome, budget to team. Ribbons draw in; hover follows a flow.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How a quantity flows and splits between stages. The thicker the ribbon, the more flows through it.
- How to read it: Read left to right. A node is a stage; each ribbon is a path from one stage to the next, with width equal to the amount. Hover a node to follow where its amount goes.
- Use it for: Traffic source to page to signup, budget to team to project, energy or money flows.
- Skip it when: Cycles (flows that loop back), or very many nodes. Keep it to about 10 nodes.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add sankey-chart`
- Import: `import { SankeyChart } from '@/components/ui/sankey-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { SankeyChart } from '@/components/ui/sankey-chart';

export default function SankeyChartDemo() {
  return (
    <SankeyChart
      className="w-[42rem] max-w-full"
      nodes={[
        { id: 'search', label: 'Search' }, { id: 'social', label: 'Social', color: 'text-success' }, { id: 'email', label: 'Email', color: 'text-warning' },
        { id: 'home', label: 'Home' }, { id: 'pricing', label: 'Pricing', color: 'text-info' }, { id: 'docs', label: 'Docs', color: 'text-success' },
        { id: 'signup', label: 'Signed up', color: 'text-success' }, { id: 'left', label: 'Left', color: 'text-destructive' },
      ]}
      links={[
        { source: 'search', target: 'home', value: 320 }, { source: 'search', target: 'docs', value: 210 },
        { source: 'social', target: 'home', value: 180 }, { source: 'social', target: 'pricing', value: 90 },
        { source: 'email', target: 'pricing', value: 140 }, { source: 'email', target: 'home', value: 40 },
        { source: 'home', target: 'signup', value: 120 }, { source: 'home', target: 'left', value: 420 },
        { source: 'pricing', target: 'signup', value: 110 }, { source: 'pricing', target: 'left', value: 120 },
        { source: 'docs', target: 'signup', value: 60 }, { source: 'docs', target: 'left', value: 150 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Saved views (`saved-views`)
Menu of saved table setups: pick one, save the current one under a name, delete.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add saved-views`
- Import: `import { SavedViews } from '@/components/ui/saved-views'`
- Also needs: button, icons, popover

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { SavedViews, type SavedView } from '@/components/ui/saved-views';

export default function SavedViewsDemo() {
  const [views, setViews] = React.useState<SavedView[]>([{ id: 'v1', name: 'My open tasks' }, { id: 'v2', name: 'Overdue invoices' }, { id: 'v3', name: 'On leave this week' }]);
  const [active, setActive] = React.useState<string>();
  return (
    <SavedViews
      views={views}
      activeId={active}
      onSelect={setActive}
      onSave={(name) => { const id = `v${Date.now()}`; setViews([...views, { id, name }]); setActive(id); }}
      onDelete={(id) => { setViews(views.filter((v) => v.id !== id)); if (active === id) setActive(undefined); }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Scatter chart (`scatter-chart`)
Scatter and bubble chart with axis labels, groups by color and a nearest-point hover. Points pop in one by one on scroll.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Each dot is one item, placed by two numbers. Bubble size can add a third, color a fourth.
- How to read it: Right means a bigger x value, higher means a bigger y. A cloud sloping up means the two numbers rise together. Dots far from the cloud are outliers. Bigger bubbles mean a bigger size value.
- Use it for: Seats vs revenue per customer, price vs rating, spotting outliers and clusters.
- Skip it when: Fewer than 10 points (use a table), or time series (use a line chart).
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add scatter-chart`
- Import: `import { ScatterChart } from '@/components/ui/scatter-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { ScatterChart, type ScatterPoint } from '@/components/ui/scatter-chart';

// Deterministic pseudo-random so the demo looks the same every time.
const rnd = (i: number) => { const x = Math.sin(i * 12.9898) * 43758.5453; return x - Math.floor(x); };

export default function ScatterChartDemo() {
  const points = React.useMemo<ScatterPoint[]>(() => Array.from({ length: 48 }, (_, i) => {
    const group = i % 3;
    const x = 10 + rnd(i) * 70 + group * 8;
    return { x: Math.round(x), y: Math.round(20 + x * (0.6 + group * 0.25) + rnd(i + 99) * 25), size: Math.round(20 + rnd(i + 7) * 180), group, label: `Account ${i + 1}` };
  }), []);
  return (
    <ScatterChart
      className="w-full max-w-xl"
      xLabel="Seats"
      yLabel="Monthly revenue (₹K)"
      groups={[{ name: 'Starter' }, { name: 'Pro' }, { name: 'Business' }]}
      points={points}
    />
  );
}
```

## Slope chart (`slope-chart`)
One line per item between two moments. Steep means big change, crossing means swapped places. Green rose, red fell.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Each item is one line between two moments in time.
- How to read it: Left dots are the earlier value, right dots the later one. A steep line changed a lot, a flat line did not. Green went up, red went down. Crossing lines swapped places.
- Use it for: Before vs after for several items, this year vs last year, survey wave 1 vs wave 2.
- Skip it when: More than about 12 items, or more than two moments. Use a line chart.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add slope-chart`
- Import: `import { SlopeChart } from '@/components/ui/slope-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { SlopeChart } from '@/components/ui/slope-chart';

export default function SlopeChartDemo() {
  return (
    <SlopeChart
      className="w-[34rem] max-w-full"
      fromLabel="2025"
      toLabel="2026"
      format={(n) => `${n}%`}
      rows={[
        { label: 'Engineering', from: 62, to: 78 }, { label: 'Sales', from: 71, to: 69 }, { label: 'Support', from: 55, to: 74 },
        { label: 'Marketing', from: 68, to: 81 }, { label: 'Finance', from: 80, to: 77 }, { label: 'People', from: 74, to: 74 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Stacked bar chart (`stacked-bar-chart`)
Bars split into colored segments that grow in on scroll, with a hover breakdown and legend. Sessions by device, revenue by plan.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Bars split into colored segments: each bar is a total, each segment is a part of it.
- How to read it: Bar height is the total for that period. Segment height is that part. Compare bottom segments directly, they all start at the same line; upper ones are harder.
- Use it for: Sessions by device per day, revenue by product per month.
- Skip it when: More than four segments, or when the middle segments matter most: they have no shared baseline, so use grouped bars or small multiples.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add stacked-bar-chart`
- Import: `import { StackedBarChart } from '@/components/ui/stacked-bar-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx

    <StackedBarChart
      className="w-full max-w-lg"
      keys={[{ key: 'mobile', label: 'Mobile' }, { key: 'desktop', label: 'Desktop', color: 'text-success' }, { key: 'tablet', label: 'Tablet', color: 'text-warning' }]}
      data={[
        { label: 'Mon', values: { mobile: 420, desktop: 310, tablet: 40 } },
        { label: 'Tue', values: { mobile: 480, desktop: 350, tablet: 52 } },
        { label: 'Wed', values: { mobile: 450, desktop: 380, tablet: 48 } },
        { label: 'Thu', values: { mobile: 520, desktop: 340, tablet: 60 } },
        { label: 'Fri', values: { mobile: 610, desktop: 290, tablet: 44 } },
        { label: 'Sat', values: { mobile: 700, desktop: 150, tablet: 38 } },
        { label: 'Sun', values: { mobile: 640, desktop: 130, tablet: 35 } },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Stream chart (`stream-chart`)
Streamgraph: smooth stacked flows around a center line to show shifts in mix over time. Ripples in from the left; hover a flow to focus it.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A smooth stacked area drawn around a center line, so shifts in mix stand out. Also called a streamgraph.
- How to read it: Each colored flow is a topic. A flow getting thicker means it grew in share. Read the width of a flow, not its height. Hover a flow to isolate it.
- Use it for: Support ticket topics over months, music genres by year, how the mix of anything shifts.
- Skip it when: Reading exact values: flows have no common baseline. Use a stacked area or a table.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add stream-chart`
- Import: `import { StreamChart } from '@/components/ui/stream-chart'`
- Also needs: area-chart, charts

Example:

```tsx
import { StreamChart } from '@/components/ui/stream-chart';

export default function StreamChartDemo() {
  return (
    <StreamChart
      className="w-full max-w-xl"
      labels={['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun', 'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct']}
      series={[
        { name: 'Billing', data: [20, 24, 30, 28, 22, 18, 16, 20, 26, 30] },
        { name: 'Login', data: [12, 14, 13, 18, 26, 34, 30, 22, 16, 14] },
        { name: 'Bugs', data: [8, 10, 14, 20, 24, 22, 28, 34, 30, 24] },
        { name: 'How-to', data: [14, 12, 11, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22] },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Sunburst chart (`sunburst-chart`)
A hierarchy as concentric rings: each ring splits its parent. Rings sweep outward; hover a slice to light up its parents and children.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A hierarchy drawn as rings. The center is the whole, and each ring out splits the one inside it.
- How to read it: Angle (how far around) is the size. Each ring is one level deeper. A slice and its children sit directly on top of each other. Hover to highlight a slice with its parents and children.
- Use it for: Spend by team then project, files by folder, categories and subcategories.
- Skip it when: Deep or lopsided trees, and when comparing exact values. A treemap or table is easier.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add sunburst-chart`
- Import: `import { SunburstChart } from '@/components/ui/sunburst-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { SunburstChart } from '@/components/ui/sunburst-chart';

export default function SunburstChartDemo() {
  return (
    <SunburstChart
      format={(n) => `₹${(n / 100000).toFixed(1)}L`}
      data={[
        { label: 'Engineering', children: [{ label: 'Web', children: [{ label: 'Frontend', value: 2200000 }, { label: 'Backend', value: 1800000 }] }, { label: 'Mobile', value: 3000000 }, { label: 'Infra', value: 2000000 }] },
        { label: 'Sales', children: [{ label: 'India', value: 3000000 }, { label: 'Middle East', value: 2000000 }] },
        { label: 'People', children: [{ label: 'Hiring', value: 900000 }, { label: 'Benefits', value: 600000 }] },
        { label: 'Marketing', children: [{ label: 'Paid', value: 1500000 }, { label: 'Content', value: 900000 }] },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Tree table (`tree-table`)
Table whose rows have child rows. Expand and collapse branches by click or arrow keys.
- Group: Data
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add tree-table`
- Import: `import { TreeTable } from '@/components/ui/tree-table'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@/components/ui/badge';
import { TreeTable, type TreeRow } from '@/components/ui/tree-table';

interface Budget extends TreeRow { name: string; owner: string; budget: number; spent: number; children?: Budget[] }

const rows: Budget[] = [
  { id: 'eng', name: 'Engineering', owner: 'Aarav Mehta', budget: 9_000_000, spent: 6_400_000, children: [
    { id: 'eng-web', name: 'Web platform', owner: 'Ananya K.', budget: 4_000_000, spent: 3_100_000, children: [
      { id: 'eng-web-fe', name: 'Frontend', owner: 'Ananya K.', budget: 2_200_000, spent: 1_800_000 },
      { id: 'eng-web-be', name: 'Backend', owner: 'Kabir Shah', budget: 1_800_000, spent: 1_300_000 },
    ] },
    { id: 'eng-mobile', name: 'Mobile', owner: 'Rohan Das', budget: 3_000_000, spent: 2_100_000 },
    { id: 'eng-infra', name: 'Infrastructure', owner: 'Kabir Shah', budget: 2_000_000, spent: 1_200_000 },
  ] },
  { id: 'sales', name: 'Sales', owner: 'Vikram Joshi', budget: 5_000_000, spent: 5_300_000, children: [
    { id: 'sales-in', name: 'India', owner: 'Vikram Joshi', budget: 3_000_000, spent: 3_400_000 },
    { id: 'sales-me', name: 'Middle East', owner: 'Isha Nair', budget: 2_000_000, spent: 1_900_000 },
  ] },
  { id: 'ops', name: 'People Ops', owner: 'Isha Nair', budget: 1_500_000, spent: 900_000 },
];
const lakh = (n: number) => `₹${(n / 100_000).toFixed(1)}L`;

export default function TreeTableDemo() {
  return (
    <TreeTable
      className="w-full"
      rows={rows}
      defaultExpanded={['eng']}
      columns={[
        { key: 'name', header: 'Department' },
        { key: 'owner', header: 'Owner' },
        { key: 'budget', header: 'Budget', align: 'end', render: (r) => lakh(r.budget) },
        { key: 'spent', header: 'Spent', align: 'end', render: (r) => lakh(r.spent) },
        { key: 'status', header: 'Status', render: (r) => (r.spent > r.budget ? <Badge variant="danger">Over</Badge> : <Badge variant="success">On track</Badge>) },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Treemap (`treemap`)
Tiles sized by value, packed to stay square. Budget by team, revenue by product. Spring in on scroll; hover lifts one tile and dims the rest.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A whole split into rectangles, where area is the amount.
- How to read it: A bigger rectangle is a bigger share. Rectangles are sorted biggest first from the top left. Hover for the exact value and percent.
- Use it for: Budget by team, revenue by product, disk space by folder.
- Skip it when: Comparing close values: area is hard to judge. Use bars. Also not for negative numbers.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add treemap`
- Import: `import { Treemap } from '@/components/ui/treemap'`
- Also needs: charts

```tsx
        { label: 'Engineering', value: 9000000 },
        { label: 'Sales', value: 5300000, color: 'text-success' },
        { label: 'Marketing', value: 3200000, color: 'text-warning' },
        { label: 'Operations', value: 2600000, color: 'text-info' },
        { label: 'People', value: 1500000 },
        { label: 'Finance', value: 1100000, color: 'text-success' },
        { label: 'Legal', value: 600000, color: 'text-warning' },
```

## Uptime bar (`uptime-bar`)
Status-page strip with one tick per day in green, amber or red, the uptime percentage and an incident note on hover.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A status-page strip: one tick per day showing if a service was healthy.
- How to read it: Green is up, amber is slow or partly down, red is down. The percentage is how much of the period was healthy. Hover a tick for the date and what happened.
- Use it for: Service status pages, monitoring dashboards.
- Skip it when: Short or irregular monitoring data. Use a line chart of response time.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add uptime-bar`
- Import: `import { UptimeBar } from '@/components/ui/uptime-bar'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { UptimeBar, type UptimeDay } from '@/components/ui/uptime-bar';

const days = (bad: Record<number, UptimeDay['status']>): UptimeDay[] => Array.from({ length: 60 }, (_, i) => ({ date: `${60 - i} days ago`, status: bad[i] ?? 'up', note: bad[i] === 'down' ? 'Outage: database failover took 22 minutes' : bad[i] === 'degraded' ? 'Slow responses for some users' : undefined }));

export default function UptimeBarDemo() {
  return (
    <div className="grid w-[36rem] max-w-full gap-6">
      <UptimeBar name="API" days={days({ 14: 'degraded', 41: 'down' })} />
      <UptimeBar name="Dashboard" days={days({ 22: 'degraded', 23: 'degraded', 58: 'degraded' })} />
      <UptimeBar name="Webhooks" days={days({})} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Venn chart (`venn-chart`)
Two or three overlapping circles with a count in every region: who is in one group, who is in several.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: Overlapping circles showing what groups share. Two or three sets.
- How to read it: Each circle is a group. The number where circles overlap is how many are in both groups. The number in the part of a circle that does not overlap is those in only that group.
- Use it for: Customers on web, app or both; skills shared between teams; audience overlap.
- Skip it when: More than three groups (circles cannot show every overlap). Use an upset plot or a table. Circle sizes here do not scale with the counts.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add venn-chart`
- Import: `import { VennChart } from '@/components/ui/venn-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { VennChart } from '@/components/ui/venn-chart';

export default function VennChartDemo() {
  return (
    <VennChart
      sets={[{ id: 'web', label: 'Web users' }, { id: 'app', label: 'App users' }, { id: 'api', label: 'API users' }]}
      values={{ web: 420, app: 310, api: 90, 'web+app': 180, 'web+api': 40, 'app+api': 35, 'web+app+api': 22 }}
    />
  );
}
```

## Virtual list (`virtual-list`)
Windowed list that renders only the visible rows. 100,000 items stay smooth.

## Waffle chart (`waffle-chart`)
A grid of 100 squares, each one percent of the whole. Squares pop in as a wave; hover a legend row to light up its squares.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: A grid of 100 squares, each one percent of the whole.
- How to read it: Count the squares of one color to read its percent. Easier to feel than a pie: "46 out of 100".
- Use it for: Survey answers, task status, budget split, progress toward a whole.
- Skip it when: More than four or five categories, or values under 1%, which vanish.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add waffle-chart`

## Waterfall chart (`waterfall-chart`)
How a start number becomes an end number: green adds, red subtracts, blue totals. Bars drop in one after another with connector lines.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: How a starting number turns into an ending number through a series of ups and downs.
- How to read it: Blue bars are totals. Green floats up from the previous level (an increase), red floats down (a decrease). Each step starts where the last one ended, joined by a thin line.
- Use it for: Revenue to profit, cash flow, headcount changes, budget variance.
- Skip it when: More than about 10 steps, or data with no meaningful running total.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add waterfall-chart`
- Import: `import { WaterfallChart } from '@/components/ui/waterfall-chart'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { WaterfallChart } from '@/components/ui/waterfall-chart';

export default function WaterfallChartDemo() {
  return (
    <WaterfallChart
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      format={(n) => `₹${n}L`}
      steps={[
        { label: 'Revenue', value: 120, total: true },
        { label: 'COGS', value: -42 },
        { label: 'Gross', value: 78, total: true },
        { label: 'Payroll', value: -31 },
        { label: 'Marketing', value: -12 },
        { label: 'Grants', value: 6 },
        { label: 'Tax', value: -9 },
        { label: 'Profit', value: 32, total: true },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Word cloud (`word-cloud`)
Words sized by how often they appear, biggest in the middle. Words grow in; hover to focus one, or make them clickable filters.
- Group: Data
- What it shows: The words used most, sized by how often they appear.
- How to read it: A bigger word was used more. Position does not matter except that the biggest words sit near the middle. Hover a word for its count.
- Use it for: Survey answers, support topics, search terms: a quick feel for what people talk about.
- Skip it when: Precise comparison (use a lollipop or bar chart) and long phrases. It also hides context, so do not use it for decisions alone.
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add word-cloud`
- Import: `import { WordCloud } from '@/components/ui/word-cloud'`
- Also needs: charts

Example:

```tsx
import { WordCloud } from '@/components/ui/word-cloud';

export default function WordCloudDemo() {
  const w = (text: string, value: number) => ({ text, value });
  return (
    <WordCloud
      className="w-[36rem] max-w-full"
      words={[w('pricing', 98), w('login', 84), w('export', 61), w('invoice', 57), w('slow', 52), w('mobile', 48), w('refund', 40), w('API', 38), w('dark mode', 33), w('SSO', 30), w('billing', 28), w('search', 24), w('import', 22), w('webhook', 19), w('GST', 17), w('crash', 15), w('reports', 14), w('onboarding', 12), w('widgets', 10), w('timezone', 9)]}
    />
  );
}
```

## Loader (`loader`)
Six loading animations (ring, dots, bars, pulse, orbit, dual), an indeterminate or determinate bar loader, and a loading overlay.
- Group: Feedback
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add loader`
- Import: `import { Loader, BarLoader, LoadingOverlay } from '@/components/ui/loader'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Card, CardContent, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card';
import { BarLoader, Loader, LoadingOverlay, type LoaderVariant } from '@/components/ui/loader';
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton';

const variants: LoaderVariant[] = ['ring', 'dots', 'bars', 'pulse', 'orbit', 'dual'];

export default function LoaderDemo() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = React.useState(true);
  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-lg gap-6">
      <div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-6">
        {variants.map((v) => (
          <div key={v} className="grid justify-items-center gap-2 rounded-lg border py-4">
            <Loader variant={v} />
            <span className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">{v}</span>
          </div>
        ))}
      </div>
      <div className="grid gap-3">
        <BarLoader />
        <BarLoader value={64} />
      </div>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" className="justify-self-start" onClick={() => setLoading((l) => !l)}>{loading ? 'Stop loading' : 'Reload report'}</Button>
      <LoadingOverlay loading={loading} label="Fetching report" variant="orbit">
        <Card>
          <CardHeader>
            <CardTitle>Monthly revenue</CardTitle>
          </CardHeader>
          <CardContent className="grid gap-2">
            <Skeleton className="h-6 w-1/3" />
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
            <Skeleton className="h-4 w-4/5" />
          </CardContent>
        </Card>
      </LoadingOverlay>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Pull to refresh (`pull-to-refresh`)
Scroll area you pull down from the top to refresh, with a spinner until your promise settles.
- Group: Feedback
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add pull-to-refresh`
- Import: `import { PullToRefresh } from '@/components/ui/pull-to-refresh'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { PullToRefresh } from '@/components/ui/pull-to-refresh';

export default function PullToRefreshDemo() {
  const [items, setItems] = React.useState(['Aarav punched in', 'Diya applied for leave', 'Payroll draft created']);
  const refresh = async () => {
    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1200));
    setItems((l) => [`New update at ${new Date().toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit', second: '2-digit' })}`, ...l]);
  };
  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-xs">
      <PullToRefresh onRefresh={refresh} className="h-64 rounded-xl border bg-card">
        <ul className="divide-y">{items.map((t, i) => <li key={t + i} className="px-4 py-3 text-[13px]">{t}</li>)}</ul>
      </PullToRefresh>
      <p className="mt-2 px-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground">Drag down from the top (touch or mouse).</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Toast (`toast`)
Call toast.success() from anywhere. No provider needed.

- Also needs: icons

```tsx

  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.success('Saved', 'Your changes are live.')}>Success</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.error('Could not save', 'Check your connection.')}>Error</Button>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => toast.info('Heads up')}>Info</Button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Alert dialog (`alert-dialog`)
Confirm before something destructive. Cancel and confirm, controlled by you.
- Group: Overlays
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add alert-dialog`
- Import: `import { AlertDialog } from '@/components/ui/alert-dialog'`
- Also needs: button, dialog, icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { AlertDialog } from '@/components/ui/alert-dialog';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { TrashIcon } from '@/components/ui/icons';
import { toast } from '@/components/ui/toast';

export default function AlertDialogDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="destructive" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}><TrashIcon /> Delete employee</Button>
      <AlertDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        destructive
        title="Delete this employee?"
        description="Their records are removed from payroll and cannot be recovered."
        confirmLabel="Delete"
        onConfirm={() => toast.success('Employee deleted')}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Sheet that rises from the bottom, with a drag handle to dismiss. Radix Dialog underneath.

```tsx
export default function BottomSheetDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Apply for leave</Button>
      <BottomSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} title="Apply for" description="Drag the handle down to dismiss.">
        <ul className="grid gap-1 pb-2">
          {options.map((o) => (
            <li key={o}><button type="button" onClick={() => { setOpen(false); toast.success('Selected', o); }} className="w-full rounded-lg px-3 py-3 text-left text-sm font-medium outline-none hover:bg-secondary focus-visible:bg-secondary">{o}</button></li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </BottomSheet>
    </>
  );
}
```

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { CalendarIcon, FileIcon, UsersIcon } from '@/components/ui/icons';

import { CommandDialog, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from '@/components/ui/command';

export default function CommandDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>
        Open palette <Kbd>⌘K</Kbd>
      </Button>
      <CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <CommandInput placeholder="Type a command or search..." />
        <CommandList>
          <CommandEmpty>No results.</CommandEmpty>
          <CommandGroup heading="People">
            <CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}><UsersIcon /> Employee directory</CommandItem>
            <CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}><CalendarIcon /> Leave calendar</CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
          <CommandGroup heading="Reports">
            <CommandItem onSelect={() => setOpen(false)}><FileIcon /> Payroll summary</CommandItem>
          </CommandGroup>
        </CommandList>
      </CommandDialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

## Context menu (`context-menu`)
Right-click menu with items, shortcuts, checkbox items, labels and nested submenus.
- Group: Overlays
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add context-menu`
- Import: `import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuTrigger, ContextMenuGroup, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut } from '@/components/ui/context-menu'`
- Also needs: icons
- npm packages: @radix-ui/react-context-menu

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { CopyIcon, DownloadIcon, FolderInputIcon, LinkIcon, EditIcon, TrashIcon } from '@/components/ui/icons';
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuCheckboxItem, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuShortcut, ContextMenuSub, ContextMenuSubContent, ContextMenuSubTrigger, ContextMenuTrigger } from '@/components/ui/context-menu';
import { toast } from '@/components/ui/toast';

export default function ContextMenuDemo() {
  const [starred, setStarred] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <ContextMenu>
        <ContextMenuTrigger asChild>
          <div className="grid h-40 w-72 cursor-context-menu place-items-center rounded-xl border border-dashed text-sm text-muted-foreground select-none">
            <div className="text-center">
              <p className="font-medium text-foreground">Q3-budget.xlsx</p>
              <p>Right-click anywhere here</p>
            </div>
          </div>
        </ContextMenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenuContent className="w-56">
          <ContextMenuLabel>Q3-budget.xlsx</ContextMenuLabel>
          <ContextMenuItem onSelect={() => toast.info('Renaming')}><EditIcon /> Rename <ContextMenuShortcut>F2</ContextMenuShortcut></ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuItem onSelect={() => toast.success('Copied')}><CopyIcon /> Duplicate <ContextMenuShortcut>⌘D</ContextMenuShortcut></ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuSub>
            <ContextMenuSubTrigger><FolderInputIcon /> Move to</ContextMenuSubTrigger>
            <ContextMenuSubContent className="w-44">
              <ContextMenuItem>Finance</ContextMenuItem>
              <ContextMenuItem>Archive</ContextMenuItem>
              <ContextMenuItem>Shared drive</ContextMenuItem>
            </ContextMenuSubContent>
          </ContextMenuSub>
          <ContextMenuCheckboxItem checked={starred} onCheckedChange={setStarred}>Starred</ContextMenuCheckboxItem>
          <ContextMenuSeparator />
          <ContextMenuItem onSelect={() => toast.success('Link copied')}><LinkIcon /> Copy link</ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuItem><DownloadIcon /> Download</ContextMenuItem>
          <ContextMenuSeparator />
          <ContextMenuItem destructive><TrashIcon /> Delete <ContextMenuShortcut>⌫</ContextMenuShortcut></ContextMenuItem>
        </ContextMenuContent>
      </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

## Image viewer (`image-viewer`)
Lightbox with arrows, click to zoom and keyboard control.
- Group: Overlays
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add image-viewer`
- Import: `import { ImageViewer } from '@/components/ui/image-viewer'`
- Also needs: icons
- npm packages: @radix-ui/react-dialog

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { ImageViewer, type ViewerImage } from '@/components/ui/image-viewer';

const art = (bg: string, fg: string, label: string) =>
  `data:image/svg+xml;utf8,${encodeURIComponent(`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1200 800"><rect width="1200" height="800" fill="${bg}"/><circle cx="820" cy="300" r="190" fill="${fg}" opacity=".85"/><rect x="180" y="420" width="520" height="220" rx="24" fill="${fg}" opacity=".55"/><text x="60" y="110" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="56" fill="${fg}">${label}</text></svg>`)}`;

const images: ViewerImage[] = [
  { src: art('#e0e7ff', '#4338ca', 'Office floor plan'), alt: 'Office floor plan' },
  { src: art('#fce7f3', '#be185d', 'Brand moodboard'), alt: 'Brand moodboard' },
  { src: art('#dcfce7', '#15803d', 'Event photos'), alt: 'Event photos' },
  { src: art('#fef3c7', '#b45309', 'Product shots'), alt: 'Product shots' },
];

export default function ImageViewerDemo() {
  const [index, setIndex] = React.useState<number | null>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <div className="grid grid-cols-4 gap-2">
        {images.map((im, i) => (
          <button key={im.alt} type="button" onClick={() => setIndex(i)} className="aspect-square w-24 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border outline-none transition-transform hover:scale-[1.03] focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/50">
            <img src={im.src} alt={im.alt} className="size-full object-cover" />
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <ImageViewer images={images} index={index} onIndexChange={setIndex} />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Popover (`popover`)
Floating panel anchored to a trigger.
- Group: Overlays
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add popover`
- Import: `import { Popover, PopoverTrigger, PopoverAnchor, PopoverContent } from '@/components/ui/popover'`
- npm packages: @radix-ui/react-popover

Example:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';
import { Field } from '@/components/ui/label';
import { Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger } from '@/components/ui/popover';

export default function PopoverDemo() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Quick add</Button>
      </PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent className="grid gap-3">
        <p className="text-sm font-semibold">New lead</p>
        <Field label="Company" htmlFor="co"><Input id="co" placeholder="Acme Pvt Ltd" /></Field>
        <Button size="sm">Add lead</Button>
      </PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  );
}
```

## Shortcuts dialog (`shortcuts-dialog`)
Keyboard cheat sheet that opens on ? and shows grouped shortcuts as keycaps.
- Group: Overlays
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add shortcuts-dialog`
- Import: `import { ShortcutsDialog } from '@/components/ui/shortcuts-dialog'`
- Also needs: dialog, kbd

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Kbd } from '@/components/ui/kbd';
import { ShortcutsDialog } from '@/components/ui/shortcuts-dialog';

export default function ShortcutsDialogDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-3">
      <Button variant="outline" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Keyboard shortcuts</Button>
      <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">or press <Kbd>?</Kbd></p>
      <ShortcutsDialog
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        groups={[
          { title: 'General', items: [{ keys: ['Ctrl', 'K'], label: 'Command palette' }, { keys: ['?'], label: 'This help' }, { keys: ['Esc'], label: 'Close dialog' }] },
          { title: 'Navigation', items: [{ keys: ['G', 'H'], label: 'Go to home' }, { keys: ['G', 'R'], label: 'Go to reports' }, { keys: ['/'], label: 'Focus search' }] },
          { title: 'Tables', items: [{ keys: ['J'], label: 'Next row' }, { keys: ['K'], label: 'Previous row' }, { keys: ['Enter'], label: 'Open row' }] },
          { title: 'Editing', items: [{ keys: ['⌘', 'S'], label: 'Save' }, { keys: ['⌘', 'Z'], label: 'Undo' }, { keys: ['Shift', '⌘', 'Z'], label: 'Redo' }] },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Tooltip (`tooltip`)
Hint on hover and focus. Optional title, keyboard shortcut, light style and arrow, plus an (i) InfoTip and a TruncatedText that only shows a tooltip when cut off.
- Group: Overlays
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add tooltip`
- Import: `import { TooltipProvider, Tooltip, InfoTip, TruncatedText } from '@/components/ui/tooltip'`
- Also needs: icons, kbd
- npm packages: @radix-ui/react-tooltip

Example:

```tsx
import { BellIcon, EditIcon, SaveIcon, Share2Icon } from '@/components/ui/icons';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { InfoTip, Tooltip, TooltipProvider, TruncatedText } from '@/components/ui/tooltip';

export default function TooltipDemo() {
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <div className="grid justify-items-center gap-5">
        <div className="flex gap-2">
          <Tooltip content="Edit"><Button variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="Edit"><EditIcon /></Button></Tooltip>
          <Tooltip content="Share" side="bottom" arrow><Button variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="Share"><Share2Icon /></Button></Tooltip>
          <Tooltip content="Notifications" side="right"><Button variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="Notifications"><BellIcon /></Button></Tooltip>
          <Tooltip content="Save changes" shortcut={['⌘', 'S']}><Button variant="outline" size="icon" aria-label="Save changes"><SaveIcon /></Button></Tooltip>
        </div>
        <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5 text-sm font-medium">
          Net 30 terms
          <InfoTip title="Payment terms" content="Invoice is due 30 days after it is issued. Late fees start on day 31." />
        </div>
        <div className="w-44 rounded-md border px-3 py-2 text-sm">
          <TruncatedText>Quarterly vendor reconciliation report, final draft</TruncatedText>
        </div>
      </div>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

## Tour (`tour`)
Spotlight a part of the page and step through it with a card, for product walkthroughs.
- Group: Overlays
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add tour`
- Import: `import { Tour } from '@/components/ui/tour'`
- Also needs: button, popover

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';
import { Tour, type TourStep } from '@/components/ui/tour';

export default function TourDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false);
  const search = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const create = React.useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const activity = React.useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

  const steps: TourStep[] = [
    { target: search, title: 'Search everything', body: 'Find people, files and settings from one box.' },
    { target: create, title: 'Create something', body: 'Start a project, invite a teammate or upload a file.' },
    { target: activity, title: 'Stay in the loop', body: 'Everything your team does shows up here.', side: 'top' },
  ];

  return (
    <div className="w-full max-w-md space-y-4">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <div ref={search} className="flex-1"><Input aria-label="Search" placeholder="Search" /></div>
        <Button ref={create} variant="outline">New project</Button>
      </div>
      <div ref={activity} className="rounded-lg border p-4 text-sm text-muted-foreground">Ada commented on Roadmap · 2 minutes ago</div>
      <Button variant="soft" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Take the tour</Button>
      <Tour steps={steps} open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

```tsx
      {zones.map(([city, tz]) => (
        <div key={tz} className="grid justify-items-center gap-2">
          <AnalogClock timeZone={tz} size={128} />
          <span className="text-sm font-medium">{city}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Event calendar (`event-calendar`)
Month view with events on their days, multi-day spans, +n more overflow, locale-aware names and RTL arrows.

- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add event-calendar`
- Import: `import { EventCalendar } from '@/components/ui/event-calendar'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { EventCalendar, type CalendarEvent } from '@/components/ui/event-calendar';
import { toast } from '@/components/ui/toast';

const d = (day: number) => { const t = new Date(); return new Date(t.getFullYear(), t.getMonth(), day); };
const events: CalendarEvent[] = [
  { id: '1', title: 'Sprint planning', start: d(3), tone: 'primary' },
  { id: '2', title: 'Diwali break', start: d(9), end: d(12), tone: 'warning' },
  { id: '3', title: 'Payroll run', start: d(15), tone: 'success' },
  { id: '4', title: 'Design review', start: d(15), tone: 'primary' },
  { id: '5', title: 'Offsite', start: d(15), end: d(16), tone: 'muted' },
  { id: '6', title: '1:1 with Meera', start: d(15), tone: 'primary' },
  { id: '7', title: 'Audit deadline', start: d(24), tone: 'destructive' },
];

export default function EventCalendarDemo() {
  return <EventCalendar className="w-full" events={events} weekStartsOn={1} onEventClick={(e) => toast.info(e.title)} />;
}
```

## Relative time (`relative-time`)
"3 minutes ago", kept live. Hover for the full date. Uses Intl, so it speaks your locale.
- Group: Time
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add relative-time`
- Import: `import { relative, RelativeTime } from '@/components/ui/relative-time'`

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { RelativeTime } from '@/components/ui/relative-time';

export default function RelativeTimeDemo() {
  const now = React.useMemo(() => Date.now(), []);
  const items = [
    ['Leave approved', now - 25000],
    ['Payslip generated', now - 14 * 60000],
    ['Review submitted', now - 5 * 3600000],
    ['Joined the team', now - 3 * 86400000],
    ['Offer expires', now + 2 * 86400000],
  ] as const;
  return (
    <ul className="w-72 divide-y rounded-xl border bg-card text-sm">
      {items.map(([t, d]) => (
        <li key={t} className="flex justify-between px-4 py-2.5"><span>{t}</span><RelativeTime date={d} className="text-muted-foreground" /></li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

## Time picker (`time-picker`)

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { TimePicker } from '@/components/ui/time-picker';

export default function TimePickerDemo() {
  const [a, setA] = React.useState('09:30');
  const [b, setB] = React.useState('17:45');
  return (
    <div className="grid justify-items-start gap-4">
      <div className="grid gap-1.5"><span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Shift starts (12-hour)</span><TimePicker value={a} onValueChange={setA} minuteStep={15} /></div>
      <div className="grid gap-1.5"><span className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Shift ends (24-hour)</span><TimePicker value={b} onValueChange={setB} hour12={false} minuteStep={15} /></div>
      <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Click a part, then use arrow keys or type. Value: {a} to {b}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Week strip (`week-strip`)
Seven day pills with previous and next week arrows, a selected day and dots under days that have something. Arrow keys move the day.
- Group: Time
- Add: `npx github:RandomKid24/befui add week-strip`
- Import: `import { WeekStrip } from '@/components/ui/week-strip'`
- Also needs: icons

Example:

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { WeekStrip } from '@/components/ui/week-strip';

export default function WeekStripDemo() {
  const [day, setDay] = React.useState(() => new Date());
  const iso = (d: Date) => `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, '0')}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, '0')}`;
  const t = new Date();
  const at = (n: number) => { const d = new Date(t); d.setDate(d.getDate() + n); return iso(d); };
  return (
    <div className="grid w-[26rem] max-w-full gap-3">
      <WeekStrip value={day} onChange={setDay} marks={{ [at(-1)]: 1, [at(0)]: 2, [at(1)]: 3, [at(3)]: true }} />
      <p className="text-center text-xs text-muted-foreground">Selected: {day.toDateString()}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```
